window.note: PROVED — an inference call logs that it started. THE STATE THIS CLOSES: the sole path to every inference host was the one boundary in the system that crossed silently. `grep -c 'emit(' cairn/devices/inference_domain/` returned ZERO before this build, and not from oversight — emit() lives on DiagnosticBase, DiagnosticBase is composed onto BaseDevice, and inference_domain HAS NO CLASS. The parent's cast phrase 'inference_domain gains an emitter' was unsatisfiable as written. WHAT SHIPPED: a private DiagnosticBase subclass declared in domain.py with one module-level instance, and one emit at each of resolve()'s three branches — miss (the one place a host is touched, carrying domain/host/path/model/provider/route_walked), hit (a boundary deliberately NOT crossed, carrying served_from), refusal (the exception type and detail, emitted after the store write, inside its own try, before the bare re-raise, so a trail failure can never impersonate a host failure). ONE LINE PER CALL AT THE OUTCOME, never one per rung: a walk is one crossing with a path, not three crossings — the grain question /intent left in unnoticed tension, decided at the cast and honoured here. THE PREMISE THE CHART OPENED ON WAS MEASURED FALSE AND THE BUILD SHRANK ACCORDINGLY: constrain's `in` list opened with 'cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py — a module-scoped trail', on orient's belief that a component without a device class cannot reach its trail. The survey drove that false at n=1, so this voyage added NOTHING under cairn/tools/ — `git diff --stat 9163ffc..HEAD -- cairn/tools/` prints nothing at acceptance. Bounds are a limit, not an obligation. SPEND CAME OFF THE TRAIL, KILLED BY A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN AN ARGUMENT: cost and the avoided counter on the hit line made BreadcrumbLog write a DEGRADED record (values {} plus values_unwritable) because a stored cost is a postgres Decimal. The fix was to CUT, not coerce — the row already holds the spend the line points at, and one number in two records can drift, which is exactly what this ticket's own agreement clause forbids. THE TRAIL SAYS WHAT THE CALL DID; THE METER SAYS WHAT IT COST — now a regression tooth. LIVE FIRE, and it is the first real record this system has ever written for an inference call: a generate against http://hex.local:11434 landed gate 'miss', home 'sent', values naming provider hex, model qwen2.5:7b, path /api/generate; the canonically-identical repeat landed gate 'hit' with served_from. Nobody wired a receiver — the default IS the mechanism. THE CHART IS ANSWERED: verdict berth /home/akien/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets/verdict-20260818T143926-ac35a04d9809.json — 7 criteria all pass, 10 hypotheses all confirmed, deposited into the hypothesize tree. Two instrument distinctions recorded rather than reworded: criterion 5's grep is OVER-WIDE (it matches CACHE_OWNER at domain.py:89, byte-identical to the BUILDME sha — the store's Law-6 owner token, a different question from the diagnostic device name), and hypothesis 7's non-vacuity instrument was SUBSTITUTED (a witness that moves the world by redirecting roots to a second temp tree and asserts the counts diverge, shipped inside the proof, instead of a hand act removing the emit). THE RE-SEAL ON THIS CROSSING IS LAW 3 DOING ITS JOB, said out loud: the PROVEME seal at 14:27:26 (fingerprint f22912926e57…) EXPIRED when the charter delta moved the component's source fingerprint to 007c64d6c6f4…. The clearance gate refused to read a closed horizon, the proof was re-run under the tester (green, 12/12, netns sealed, instance seal sealed, wrote_to_instance count 0) and re-sealed at 14:40:13. The verdict artifact's criterion-3 evidence quotes the EARLIER seal and fingerprint; it is a true dated reading, superseded by this one, and the cause was a charter write, not a code change. WHAT THIS BUILD REPRODUCED AND MADE WORSE, carried because it is the finding a reader needs: running the six standing device proofs BARE mid-build wrote 24 records into the LIVE trail (14 miss / 6 hit / 4 refused, every miss naming host 'fake-host', inside 0.3 seconds) and spoiled this ticket's own before-witness — ticket a-proof-cannot-seed-the-tree-it-reads, reproduced by the voyage that depends on it. Censused, moved aside through bin/cmd/trash, witness re-taken. And measured under the seal: test_inference_domain.py now reports wrote_to_instance count 1, path 'logs/inference_domain/0/diagnostics.jsonl' — a proof that never touched the logs tree writes to it as of today, and only the instance seal keeps it out of the live one. STANDING CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS DEVICE: a proof of inference_domain must be run UNDER THE TESTER, never bare, because its probe reads the live trail against the live store and a bare run feeds that instrument false population. WHAT THIS IS NOT: done here means inference_domain logs ITS crossings, not that the system has logs. The parent's other children are untouched — the shim's probe crossings (BaseShim at cairn/tools/base/shim.py declares no DiagnosticBase), the 30-day sweep, and two siblings still uncast. And Akien's live ground loop (pid 973171) still writes to ~/.cairn/logs/ground_loop_nohup.log rather than logs/ground_loop/0/.
